title_en: The Means That Help with Standing in Prayer at Night
body_ar:
ما هي الوسائل المعينة على قيام الليل؟

أن منها أولا أن يدرك الإنسان قيمة قيام الليل وأثره الإيماني عليه، وأن يدرك أن الله تعالى يضحك للقائم في جوف الليل، وأن يدرك أثر ذلك عليه هو، فمن حسن عمله بالليل حسن وجهه بالنهار، وأن يدرك كذلك الفرق بين حال القائم الذي يصلي ويناجي الله تعالى والناس نيام وحال النائم الذي يغط على فراشه، فالصلاة خير من النوم، وكذلك عليه أن يستعين على قيام الليل بنوم جزء من النهار أيا كان، ينام قليلا من النهار، أو بنوم أول الليل، إذا صلى العشاء فنام فلا بد أن يستيقظ في وسط الليل أو آخره، وهو أفضله فناشئة الليل هي التي أمر الله بالقراءة فيها فقال: {إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطئا وأقوم قيلا}،

وكذلك ينبغي أن يستعين عليه بآلة كالمنبه سواء كان في التلفون أو في الساعة ينبهه ويوقظه في ذلك الوقت، وكذلك يستعين عليه بأهله فقد أخرج أبو داود في السنن أن النبي (ص) قال: (رحم الله رجلا قام من الليل ليصلي فأيقظ امرأته لتصلي معه فإن هي نامت نضح في وجهها من الماء، ورحم الله امرأة قامت من الليل لتصلي فأيقظت زوجها ليصلي معها أو بعلها ليصلي معها فإن هو نام نضحت في وجهه من الماء)، ثم كذلك الاستعانة بالجيران وهذا من التعاون على البر والتقوى، فإذا كنت تتعاهد جارك وحصلت بينكما مودة وألفة فسألته أن يتعاون معك على قيام الليل وأن يطرق عليك الباب عند الساعة الفلانية ويتعاهدك فهذا مما كان أصحاب رسول الله (ص) يفعلونه، فكان سلمان يأتي أبا الدرداء وكان أبو الدرداء يقوم الليل كله فأمسكه سلمان فقال نم الآن، فلما كان نصف الليل قال قم الآن، فهذا النوع مما يتعاهد فيه الجيران ويعين بعضهم به بعضا.
body_en:
What are the means that help with standing in prayer at night?

Among them, first, that a person should grasp the worth of standing in prayer at night and its effect upon his faith; and that he should grasp that God, exalted, laughs at the one who stands in the depth of the night; and that he should grasp the effect of that upon himself — for whoever's work is good by night, his face is good by day. And likewise that he should grasp the difference between the state of the one who stands praying and speaking intimately with God, exalted, while people are asleep, and the state of the sleeper snoring on his bed: prayer is better than sleep. Likewise he must seek help for standing at night by sleeping a part of the day, whatever part it may be — he sleeps a little of the day — or by sleeping at the beginning of the night: if he prays the night prayer and then sleeps, he is bound to wake in the middle of the night or at its end, which is the best part of it; for the night vigil (nāshiʾat al-layl) is what God commanded recitation in, saying: {Truly the vigil of the night is stronger in tread and more upright in speech} (Sūrat al-Muzzammil 73:6).

Likewise he ought to seek help in it with an instrument such as an alarm, whether on the telephone or on a clock, which alerts him and wakes him at that hour. And likewise he should seek help in it from his household. Abu Dawud brought out in the Sunan that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'God have mercy on a man who rises in the night to pray and wakes his wife so that she may pray with him — and if she sleeps on, he sprinkles water on her face. And God have mercy on a woman who rises in the night to pray and wakes her husband so that he may pray with her — or her spouse so that he may pray with her — and if he sleeps on, she sprinkles water on his face.' Then likewise seeking help from the neighbours, and this is part of cooperating in righteousness and God-consciousness. If you keep up with your neighbour and there has come to be affection and familiarity between you, and you ask him to cooperate with you in standing at night, and to knock at your door at such and such an hour and keep you to it — this is among the things the Companions of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to do. Salman would come to Abu al-Darda, and Abu al-Darda used to stand the whole night in prayer; so Salman held him back and said: 'Sleep now.' Then when it was the middle of the night he said: 'Rise now.' This is the kind of thing in which neighbours keep up with one another and each helps the other.

flags.context: the close of the comparison between the one standing in prayer and the sleeper
options: render as the Sheikh's own sentence, unmarked
render and mark it as the formula of the dawn call to prayer
render in quotation marks as a quotation
flags.note: The clause is word for word the formula of the dawn call to prayer, al-ṣalātu khayrun min al-nawm, and an Arabic listener hears the allusion immediately. The Sheikh does not mark it as a quotation and neither does the English, but an English reader will hear nothing. A reviewer should decide whether the site glosses it; nothing has been added to the body.

flags.arabic: أن الله تعالى يضحك للقائم في جوف الليل
flags.context: the second of the things a person should grasp
options: that God, exalted, laughs at the one who stands in the depth of the night
that God, exalted, is pleased with the one who stands in the depth of the night
that God, exalted, smiles upon the one who stands in the depth of the night
flags.note: The Sheikh is alluding to a prophetic report and uses its verb, yaḍḥaku. This is a divine attribute report, and how it is rendered engages the creedal question of how such reports are treated — which is precisely why it should not be paraphrased into 'is pleased with' or 'smiles upon', both of which quietly interpret it. The literal rendering has been kept. The Sheikh gives no attribution and none has been supplied.

flags.arabic: فأيقظت زوجها ليصلي معها أو بعلها ليصلي معها
flags.context: within the hadith quoted from Abu Dawud
options: preserve the doubled wording as the source has it, as a transmission variant
render once and drop the duplicate
flags.note: The clause is given twice with two different words for 'husband', zawj and baʿl. This is most likely the narrator's own variant wording preserved within the transmission — the collections do record it this way — rather than a copying error, so it has been kept in both Arabic and English. Flagged so that a reviewer can confirm rather than a later editor silently tidy it.

flags.arabic: فكان سلمان يأتي أبا الدرداء … فأمسكه سلمان
flags.context: the story of Salman and Abu al-Darda
options: render as the Sheikh gives it, without attribution
flags.note: The Sheikh gives this well-known account of the two Companions with no narrator, no collection and no grading, and in a noticeably compressed form — the fuller versions include Abu al-Darda's fasting and the Prophet's endorsement, neither of which appears here. Nothing has been supplied or filled in.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-23 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The Qur'anic quotation carries no reference in the source; the reference has been supplied per house style. The wording matches Sūrat al-Muzzammil 73:6.
nāshiʾat al-layl has been kept in transliteration alongside 'the night vigil' because it is the verse's own term and the Sheikh builds his point on it.
The Sheikh attributes the hadith on waking one's spouse to Abu Dawud's Sunan. That attribution has been kept exactly as he gives it; he supplies no grading and none has been added.

'The telephone' renders al-tilfūn as the source has it; the mention of a phone alarm is the one detail in this slice that indicates the answer is of recent date, which is worth noting against the CMS date problem.
